statement: Let n ≥ 3, d = n−2, k = n−1, and ω = |Sn−1|. Let (E, h) be a connected complete enclosing-set exterior: the end-containing closed region outside a filled set, with its compact full frontier Σ included. For p, q ∈ E, define the possibly extended rectifiable-path distance dE(p, q) = inf{Lengthh(γ) : γ ⊂ E is a rectifiable path joining p to q}, inf ∅ = +∞. Completeness means that every finite-distance equivalence class {q ∈ E : dE(p, q) < ∞} is complete for the restricted metric. All points and components of Σ remain in E, and their full perimeter is counted. This convention neither identifies E with the length completion of its open exterior nor asserts finite-length access from the end to every singular frontier point. Assume that the ambient metric h is smooth on E and through Σ, and that the following conditions hold: 1. There is one Euclidean coordinate end with compact complement, and h − δ = O2(r−τ ) for some τ > d/2. 2. The scalar curvature satisfies Rh ≥ 0, Rh ∈ L1(E, dVh), and Rh = O(r−n−β) on the end for some β > 0. 3. The full frontier Σ is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing as the boundary of the filled side. Its regular part is a smooth embedded minimal hypersurface, and its singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most n − 8. Then, with A the reduced-boundary perimeter of Σ, counting every component, mADM(h) ≥ 1 2 (︃ A ω )︃d/k . The assertion includes A = 0 and requires neither a spin assumption nor connectedness of Σ.
